_comment: Widget example data, loaded at boot by WidgetRegistry from the hardcoded path
core logs '[Widget Registry] Manifest not found ... skipping widget examples' to stderr on
every start and the widget-examples MCP resource is empty.
`uri` MUST be ui://widget/next-<route>.html — that is Component.getUri()
(core/component.js:116) applied to the id createComponentFromNextRoute derives as
`next-<routePath>`. A mismatched uri silently registers an example nothing can look up.
The payloads below are real, trimmed outputs for PIQ-2026-2001 (the RING-ALPHA demo
subject), so an inspector previewing a widget shows the fraud ring rather than a blank frame.

widgets.name: Risk Graph
widgets.description: Applicant link-analysis graph. Nodes are applications coloured by risk level, edges are the identifiers they share. Rendered from build_risk_graph output.

examples.name: RING-ALPHA — four linked applicants
examples.description: Vikram Nair's cluster: a reused document photograph, address, phone, email and passport number spanning four applications.

clusterSummary.headline: Vikram Nair is linked to 3 other applicants by reused address, reused document photo, reused email address, reused passport number and reused phone number. The overlap pattern is consistent with a coordinated group, not coincidence.

widgets.name: Officer Dashboard
widgets.description: Verification pipeline timeline for one application, with per-stage status and whether the officer decision gate has opened. Rendered from run_verification_pipeline output.

examples.name: Completed pipeline — decision unlocked
examples.description: All nine required stages complete for PIQ-2026-2001; the optional visual_similarity_flag stage is skipped, which does not block the decision.

stages.detail: Optional stage — pass compareToApplicationId to run it.

widgets.name: Agent Console
widgets.description: The autonomous agent's reasoning trace: every observe-think-act turn it took, the tool it chose, its confidence, and the terminal handoff to a human officer. Rendered from agent_investigate / agent_triage_queue / get_agent_trace output.

examples.name: Investigation run — escalated to a human
examples.description: The agent chose its own tool sequence for PIQ-2026-2001, found the ring, and stopped at a handoff. Note that no step calls officer_decide: it is not in the agent's action allow-list.

steps.thought: Nothing is known about this application yet. Validate the submitted documents before trusting anything read off them.
Documents are valid, so the identifiers on them are worth correlating against the rest of the live queue.
steps.observation: 5 reused identifier(s) found against 3 other live applications: phone, address, document photo, email, passport number.

steps.thought: Five shared identifiers across three applications is not coincidence. Build the graph to see the shape of the cluster.
steps.observation: Cluster of 4 with density 1.0 — every member shares an identifier with every other. Consistent with a coordinated group.

steps.thought: The pattern is established. Score it against the cited rulebook so the finding is defensible rather than my opinion.
steps.observation: 3 rule(s) fired, worst severity high: DUP-010, GRF-020, DOC-004.

steps.thought: Rules fired at high severity. Produce the score and hand this to a human — I have no authority to decide it.
steps.observation: Handed off with a reject recommendation and a 4-item officer checklist.

handoff.rationale: Five identifiers are reused across four applications with full cluster density. The reused document photograph in particular cannot be explained by a shared household or a data-entry error.
officerChecklist: Compare the document photograph on PIQ-2026-2001 and PIQ-2026-2004 side by side — they hash identically.
Confirm whether the shared address is a genuine joint residence or an accommodation address.
Check whether the reused passport number belongs to an already-issued document.
Decide whether the other three cluster members should be suspended pending review.

widgets.name: Risk Explanation
widgets.description: Officer-readable explanation of the risk score and the findings that produced it. Rendered from explain_risk output (Backend A).

examples.name: High risk — coordinated ring
examples.description: Explanation for PIQ-2026-2001, driven by the duplicate-signal and graph rules.

data.explanation: Vikram Nair's application scored 74/100 (high risk) on 3 finding(s).
evidence: DUP-010: 5 high-severity duplicate signal(s) against other applications — reused identifiers indicate possible identity fraud.
GRF-020: Applicant sits in a densely connected cluster sharing multiple identifier types — consistent with a coordinated group rather than coincidence.
Vikram Nair is linked to 3 other applicants by reused address, reused document photo, reused email address, reused passport number and reused phone number.
